like enter , and respects macos-option-as-alt . #13205 macOS: Update pill fixes: update errors are now shown, "Install and Relaunch" no longer asks for confirmation, and the cancel option is hidden once an update can no longer be canceled. #13540 #13562 #13612 macOS: The default app icon follows the system icon style again after changing it in System Settings, and custom icons now apply to the app in Finder. #12180 #12344 macOS: The dock icon bell badge now appears when notification permission was granted earlier without badge permission. #12133 macOS: The Copy menu item is disabled when nothing is selected. #12521 macOS: Menu items now show the correct shortcut for keybinds on physical keys (e.g. super+backquote ), uppercase letters, forward delete, and the scroll_to_selection and search_selection actions. #13888 #12039 #12011 #12281 macOS: The secure input indicator's popover arrow now points at the icon. #12249 macOS: Fix a rare permanent freeze after waking from sleep or changing displays. macOS did not mark the app as "Not Responding", so it could only be killed. #14691 macOS: Fix a crash when closing a tab, most easily triggered with undo-timeout = 0 . #13359 #13364 macOS: Fix a crash when opening a new tab from a native fullscreen window. #13636 macOS: Fix a crash caused by a data race when reading cached terminal contents. #13646 macOS: Fix a crash when OSC 52 clipboard confirmation prompts overlap. #13648 macOS: Fix crashes when CoreText returns null, such as for fonts without a display name or under severe memory pressure. #13642 #13679 macOS: Fix closed windows leaking with transparent titlebars (the default), which made Ghostty and WindowServer use more CPU and memory over time. #13601 macOS: Fix a memory leak each time Ghostty reads terminal text, such as for copy, Quick Look, or accessibility. #12020 #12025 macOS: Fix an IOSurface memory leak when scripts rapidly create and close terminals. #13640 macOS: Fix a Mach port leak, and a gradual slowdown, while global keybinds wait for Accessibility permission. #13590 GTK (Linux, FreeBSD) GTK: Splits can now be rearranged with drag and drop, matching macOS. Drag a split by its handle and drop it onto another split, including splits in other tabs and windows. #10224 #10423 GTK: Ghostty now renders at the true fractional scale (e.g. 125% or 150%), so text and box-drawing characters are sharp instead of blurry under fractional scaling. #1938 #14269 GTK: The renderer no longer uses GtkGLArea . Ghostty now renders with EGL entirely on the render thread and hands finished frames to GTK as DMABUFs, so the main thread no longer does any OpenGL work. #14052 #14636 GTK: Windows can now be renamed using the menu, command palette, or the new prompt_window_title and set_window_title binding actions. #10469 #10999 GTK: A new +new-tab CLI command opens a new tab in a running Ghostty instance. When run from inside Ghostty, the tab opens in the same window. It accepts the same -e , --working-directory , and --title flags as +new-window . #11762 GTK: A new +toggle-quick-terminal CLI command toggles the quick terminal of a running Ghostty instance, useful for binding in window managers without global shortcut support. #12661 GTK: Global keybinds now use the vicinae-hotkey-v1 Wayland protocol when the compositor supports it (e.g. Hyprland 0.56+), falling back to the XDG desktop portal otherwise. Ghostty shows a desktop notification if a global keybind can't be registered. #13464 GTK: quick-terminal-screen is now supported on Wayland. The default, main , places the quick terminal on the compositor's primary output (or the first monitor if the compositor doesn't report one). Set it to mouse to let the compositor choose, which was the previous behavior. #11117 GTK: On Wayland, background-blur now uses the compositor-agnostic ext-background-effect-v1 protocol instead of KDE's blur protocol, enabling blur on compositors such as Niri. The blur region also no longer covers the window's client-side shadows. #10721 #10720 #10727 GTK: On GTK 4.23.3 and newer, background-blur uses GTK's built-in background blur, which covers the window more accurately. #13581 #13586 GTK: The open_config binding action now accepts new_window to edit the configuration in $VISUAL or $EDITOR in a new Ghostty window. The default, os_open , keeps the previous behavior. #11905 GTK: A new configuration gtk-horizontal-tab-scroll (default true ) can be set to false to stop two-finger horizontal scrolling from switching tabs, passing the scroll to the terminal application instead. #12659 GTK: A new configuration gtk-tabs-inverted moves the close button to the start of each tab, in both the tab bar and the tab overview. #14657 GTK: The default command palette entries are now translatable. #11641 GTK: The embedded Noto emoji fonts were updated, so newer emoji and ZWJ sequences such as the head-shaking faces render as one glyph instead of overlapping neighboring cells. #14047 GTK: ctrl+shift+page_up and ctrl+shift+page_down now move the current tab left and right ( move_tab ), matching Firefox, GNOME Terminal, and VS Code. jump_to_prompt moved to ctrl+shift+arrow_up and ctrl+shift+arrow_down . #4998 #12458 GTK: URLs now open through the XDG desktop portal, falling back to xdg-open if the portal is unavailable. Ghostty passes an activation token so the opened application, such as your browser, can come to the front on compositors that require one. #5991 #11754 #14785 #14787 GTK: Desktop notifications are now withdrawn when their terminal is focused or closed, and repeated notifications with the same text replace each other, matching macOS. #14108 GTK: Tabs that aren't visible no longer render, saving CPU and GPU. This matches macOS. #12760 GTK: The Dolphin "Open Ghostty Here" action now opens a new window in the running Ghostty instance instead of launching a separate one. #11614 GTK: Fix Ghostty sometimes failing to launch with systemd 262, which refused to start the service because Ghostty reported readiness before it could handle reload signals. #14398 #14399 GTK: Fix deeply nested splits sometimes becoming invisible or losing focus. #11193 #12698 GTK: Resizing splits, especially with resize_split keybinds, no longer flickers. #13414 GTK: resize_split on nested splits no longer causes large jumps in size. #12699 GTK: Splits can no longer be resized smaller than one cell, by dragging the divider or with resize_split . #14476 GTK: High-resolution scroll wheels no longer scroll much faster than standard scroll wheels. #12483 GTK: Disable unwanted kinetic scrolling on trackpads with GTK versions older than 4.20.1. #11793 GTK: Middle clicks are once again sent to terminal applications using mouse reporting when gtk-enable-primary-paste is disabled in GSettings. #12940 #13108 GTK: The quick terminal no longer breaks when toggled off manually while quick-terminal-autohide is enabled. #11679 #12471 GTK: Opening the right-click context menu no longer hides the quick terminal when quick-terminal-autohide is enabled. #12843 GTK: The resize overlay no longer keeps reappearing when the scrollbar is visible and no longer blocks mouse input while shown. #11970 #11972 GTK: The maximum window size is now based on the monitor the window is currently on, not the monitor it was opened on. #13171 GTK: +new-window -e now works when shell-integration is set to a specific shell. +new-window and +new-tab also accept a new --shell-integration flag. #12378 #13741 GTK: Keys remapped to modifiers with XKB (e.g. Delete remapped to ISO_Level3_Shift ) no longer also send the original key. #13967 GTK: On Wayland, the IME candidate window now follows the cursor while composing and no longer covers the line being edited. #14729 GTK: Splits in a tab that was moved to another window now act on the new window (e.g. toggle_fullscreen ). #14474 GTK: The mouse cursor keeps its text shape while selecting text. #14558 GTK: The command palette now uses the terminal colors when window-theme = ghostty . #14662 GTK: Opening URLs no longer fails when the fallback opener ( xdg-open ) produces large output. #12797 GTK: Clicking a desktop notification no longer focuses the wrong terminal when the one that sent it has since been closed. #12028 GTK: A bell in the focused terminal no longer leaves the bell indicator set. #13597 GTK: Fix the window continuously redrawing in the background after an indeterminate progress bar (OSC 9;4) was removed. #14704 #14738 GTK: Log missing or invalid gtk-xft-dpi values once instead of repeatedly. #14410 #14085 #14434 GTK: Fix a crash when closing tabs or splits on GTK 4.20 (GNOME 49). #12426 GTK: Fix a crash with global keybinds or on configuration reload when no D-Bus connection is available. #13101 GTK: Fix a possible crash when Fontconfig reports a font's language as a plain string instead of a language set. #14853 GTK: Fix a leak where every audio bell started a new GStreamer pipeline and threads that were never cleaned up, slowly raising CPU usage. #13647 #12815 #13657 Snap: Link the system FreeType, Fontconfig, HarfBuzz, libpng, and zlib instead of bundled copies, fixing frequent crashes caused by two copies of the same library in one process. #14392 #14682 Snap: The snap's own GIO modules and XDG data directories now take priority over the host's. #12045 Snap: Programs running inside Ghostty, such as clear , now find the xterm-ghostty terminfo entry. #12662 Flatpak: Commands started by Ghostty on the host are now terminated if Ghostty crashes. #12427 Localization Ghostty 1.4 introduces full localization for the command palette and adds support for 4 new languages : Basque Belarusian Danish Serbian (Cyrillic and Latin scripts) Localization is maintained by volunteer contributors. If you want to help localize Ghostty in your language, please open a discussion on the GitHub repo. Thank you to all the volunteers who contributed to Ghostty's localization! Changes for Package Maintainers Ghostty now requires Zig 0.17 to build. #14518 #14519 GTK builds now require GTK 4.18 and libadwaita 1.7 , up from GTK 4.14 and libadwaita 1.5. Builds against older headers fail at compile time, and Ghostty exits at startup if older libraries are loaded at runtime. #14330 GTK builds now link the system EGL library (pkg-config egl , usually provided by libglvnd or Mesa) for the new renderer. At runtime, Ghostty uses GTK's EGL display when it can, and otherwise needs an EGL driver that supports the surfaceless platform. #14052 #14636 A new -Dinstalled-exe-path build option sets the absolute executable path written into the desktop file, D-Bus services, and systemd user service. Previously this path came from the install prefix. Without the option, these files now name ghostty alone, which systemd only finds in /usr/bin or /usr/local/bin , so set it for any other prefix. #14805 #14806 When linking the system gtk4-layer-shell ( -fsys=gtk4-layer-shell ), version 1.0.4 or newer is now required. Ghostty no longer disables the quick terminal on older versions, which can crash on some compositors. #11559 Libghostty As with 1.3, libghostty isn't directly part of the Ghostty 1.4 release. But a large part of the 1.4 development cycle went into libghostty, so here's an update. Over the past 6 months, the C API for libghostty-vt has grown from a parser and a few encoders into a complete terminal emulator API, adopted by dozens of free and commercial terminal emulators used by millions of people. It's hard to quantify exactly, but the number of people using a libghostty-based terminal is confidently several times the number of people using the Ghostty GUI. libghostty-vt now builds for macOS, Linux, Windows (MSVC and GNU), FreeBSD, Android, iOS, and WebAssembly, and CI continuously verifies every one of these targets. The goal is for libghostty-vt to be generally usable everywhere, within reason, so if you want more target support, let us know! It's also easier to integrate libghostty-vt into existing build systems. There's CMake support, Nix packaging, an xcframework, and a source tarball, in addition to the existing pkg-config file. libghostty-vt no longer needs libc++, and it can build freestanding. The API is still marked as a work in progress and broke compatibility several times during this cycle, so expect more breaking changes before a tagged release. The API documentation and the Zig, C, C++, Swift, and WebAssembly examples (now over 30) are kept up to date with main . We're going to do a final pass over the C API, break ABI one more time, and then likely tag a libghostty 1.0 release very soon. Financial Update Ghostty is a non-profit project , fiscally sponsored by Hack Club . All of our finances are public on HCB , so you can see exactly where every dollar goes. During the 1.4 cycle, we paid $41,820 to contributors under contract and spent about $1,260 on infrastructure such as website hosting. I'm happy to share that we've now signed our first two 12-month contracts , which give contributors stable, long-term paid work on Ghostty and help ensure the ongoing stability and sustainability of the project: @trag1c is Ghostty's head of operations. He manages the community on GitHub and Discord, coordinates our volunteer translators, and maintains various other important project systems. @vancluever works on various Ghostty subsystems. In this cycle, he led the upgrade to Zig 0.16, moved the build off Zig's deprecated @cImport , updated the bundled Fontconfig, and more. He's also the author of z2d , the 2D graphics library Ghostty uses to draw box-drawing characters and other sprite glyphs. If you'd like to support Ghostty, please visit our sponsorship page . Roadmap The primary focus of the roadmap continues to be libghostty functionality, stability, and portability. During the last release cycle, I said I aimed to tag a libghostty release. We haven't done that yet, but I'm confident we will do so before Ghostty 1.5. libghostty is a project that continues to be the tide that lifts all boats. libghostty improvements tie directly to Ghostty GUI improvements as well as dozens of other large projects in the ecosystem. As more large projects adopt libghostty, libghostty tends to get more testing and attention, and this creates a cycle that yields the most gain for terminal emulators everywhere. macOS and GTK builds of Ghostty have talented, capable maintainer teams that are continuing to improve them, so they're not neglected by any means! As a project, we've decided to drop any roadmap for Windows support in the Ghostty GUI. libghostty fully supports Windows (and we test it in CI), and the official stance now is that downstream projects should use that. Our release cycle remains 6 months. This release was delayed by one month, but Ghostty 1.5 is planned for March 2027. libghostty will have a separate release cycle. new generation of world simulation Raia Hadsell, Diego Rivas and Hang Qi Join the Genie 4 waitlist Share Copied Your browser does not support the video tag. Your browser does not support the video tag. Today, we are announcing Genie 4, our new world model, which unlocks unprecedented realism and improves real-time interactive simulation. Genie 4 is natively multimodal, enabling audio-like music, ambient noises, and interactive dialogue to be simultaneously generated with the world. The Genie 4 model incorporates and builds on capabilities from the Gemini family: Gemini Omni anchors the simulations in real-world appearance and behavior, while other Gemini models provide the complex reasoning needed to help maintain a simulationâs coherence and continuity. With this foundation, you can set an event in motion, and Genie 4 simulates what happens next: how the world responds, how it sounds, and how the people in it move, react, and speak. Understanding and simulating the world is a crucial aspect of building AGI. Genie 4 advances our ability to create safe, infinitely variable simulations that can help with everything from developing training environments for robots and agents to unlocking the creation of new interactive experiences. Your browser does not support the video tag. We have started rolling Genie 4 out as a research preview for trusted testers â gathering feedback before we release it to consumers and developers, starting with Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early access partners of the Gemini API and Google AI Studio. Join the waitlist for Genie 4 in Project Genie here . Your browser does not support the video tag. Your browser does not support the video tag. Genie 4 delivers enhanced photorealism, fluid movement, and native audio. All accompanying sounds featured above are produced directly by Genie 4. Genie 4 advances four key capabilities The following are recordings of real-time interactions from Genie 4, where users use standard keyboard controls for navigation and camera control, and text prompts to steer the scene as it evolves. Shaping world simulation in real-time With Genie 4, you can use natural language to modify a simulation in real-time â like changing the weather, moving the camera, or introducing a new person or object â and Gemini will contextually adapt your prompt to match the surrounding scene. Between your inputs, Gemini also monitors and steers the scene to keep the world progressing cohesively. Turn on audio to hear Genie 4 worlds. Pushing the frontier in realism for physics and human action Genie 4 introduces a new standard of realism to real-time interactive simulation. Built on an advanced physical understanding of the world, Genie 4 simulates real-world physics scenarios, such as aerodynamics, collisions, and more. The most dramatic leap is how Genie 4 simulates people, creating characters that move naturally, respond organically to their environments, and can be interactively steered in real-time. Simulating complex events with Gemini models Bringing Gemini and Genie 4 together adds a new layer of reasoning to world simulation, allowing us to model complex, multi-step events and test how AI systems navigate different environments before bringing them to the real world. To achieve this in real-time, Gemini 3.8 Flash serves as a guiding agent in the loop: as Genie 4 generates a world in real-time, Gemini continuously observes the scene, breaks down goals into a sequence of steps, and reviews incoming frames to track the progress and verify that each step succeeded. As the world shifts or the user intervenes, Gemini adapts its plan in the moment, unlocking worlds with reliable causality, procedural behaviors, and multi-step reasoning. The wand displays fine wood grain, tiny varnish micro-cracks, cold metallic brass inlays, and tactile surface wear from handling. Porcelain Menagerie & Room Architecture: A suffocating, baroque-style gallery packed floor-to-ceiling with thousands of fragile, life-sized and miniature glazed porcelain animals. Glistening ceramic peacocks with intricate feather patterns and vibrant cobalt and emerald enamels, regal porcelain dogs, and curled porcelain cats perched on marble mantels, mahogany display shelves, and velvet-draped pedestals. The surfaces showcase authentic high-gloss ceramic glazing, micro-crazing cracks in the enamel, delicate bone china translucency, and natural dust gathering in the crevices. Cinematic Optics & Lighting: Shot on high-end anamorphic 35mm film lenses. Natural optical characteristics featuring shallow depth of field, subtle barrel distortion, realistic optical lens flares, fine organic film grain, and creamy bokeh in the background. Natural daylight streams through tall, grime-streaked Victorian lace curtains, casting soft volumetric dust motes and creating sharp, physically accurate specular highlights across the glossy curved porcelain glazes. Dynamic Movement & Physical Interaction: Continuous, smooth handheld POV traversal. The player subtly sweeps and points the wand toward the ceramic figures, causing realistic micro-vibrations in the frame as footsteps tread across creaking hardwood floorboards. The figures remain frozen in immaculate, fragile stillness, catching shifting highlights as the wand moves. Acoustic Atmosphere: Raw, immersive documentary-grade audio. Faint floorboard creaks underfoot, distant room tone, quiet breathing, the subtle dry friction of fingers adjusting their grip on the wooden wand, and the delicate, crystalline clinking resonance of fine porcelain vibrating faintly in the quiet air. A real magician stands beside a tall wooden table. On the table is a large rectangular wooden box, completely open at the top, with no lid. A real peacock stands calmly inside the box. Exceptional production design, sophisticated art direction, cinematic lighting, natural but carefully controlled light, realistic skin tones, beautiful contrast, subtle shadows, rich textures, elegant composition, shallow depth of field, high-end cinema camera, realistic human actors, extremely photorealistic. It should look like a frame from a prestigious, beautifully shot modern TV series: understated, expensive, cinematic and completely believable. No theater, no stage, no fantasy, no cartoon, no plastic-looking people, no CGI look. Your browser does not support the video tag. Your browser does not support the video tag. Prompt: crowned crane walks across the snow beneath the clear dusk gradient sky. Natural colors in a documentary style. As part of exploring this capability, we have also been experimenting with Gemini 4 Argon and Genie 4 to bring our frontier research together with Gemini Robotics . In the example below, Argon breaks down a user-instructed task into steps for Genie to render. These steps are interleaved as text captions to Genie 4 as the simulation is rendering. Because Genie 4 can be steered in real-time with text captions using Gemini, this now unlocks the path of adapting the simulation as it progresses towards the completion of that task. This capability becomes a path for simulating a breadth of scenarios in imagined worlds, using Gemini 4 Argon and Genie 4. Your browser does not support the video tag. Your browser does not support the video tag. Gemini 4 Argon and Genie 4 work together to simulate Apptronik's Apollo humanoid playing a game of checkers, breaking the task down into real-time steps. Learnings from trusted testers While Genie 4 is a major research milestone, it remains an early, experimental model. To understand how interactive world models can support real-world workflowsâand where they still need to growâweâve been working with cohorts of trusted testers across creative industries, journalism, education, gaming, and engineering. Testers highlighted how the leap in photorealism, native audio, and real-time steering allows ideas and concepts to be turned into realistic simulations, unlocking new abilities across disciplines: Creative direction : Creatives and technologists are testing Genie 4 as a rapid "draft mode" for pre-visualization and ideation. For example, filmmakers can step into a live simulation of a scene and run multiple "takes" in real-time, adjusting camera angles, lighting, dialogue, and action on the fly. Historical scenarios & immersive photographs : Photojournalists are exploring how a single 2D archival photograph can become a grounded simulation of that environment in seconds. Teams are testing how populated, dynamic worlds can help experience historical spaces or visualize how short-term environmental events, like a flash flood or wildfire, unfold. Interactive experience concept design : Game developers and creative technologists are testing Genie 4 to go from an initial idea to an explorable prototype in seconds, testing visual styles, material aesthetics, and interactive mechanics through natural language prompts before writing a single line of engine code. Simulation : Aside from our robotics research, enterprise partners across industries are evaluating Genie 4 as a tool for rapid "zero-to-one" scenario generation, and identifying gaps to further improve Genie to best fulfill that simulation need. Future work: Towards hybrid world models A promising path for future progress lies in hybrid world models, which combine the logical, structured reasoning of code and language models with the rich, sensory representation of pixel-level simulation. Bringing Genie and Gemini models closer together is an early step in this direction. Gemini works behind the scenes to map the structure and plan the narrative timeline, while Genie generates the immediate physical realityârendering how the world looks, sounds, and responds, pixel by pixel. Together, these complementary strengths can unlock a new class of world models that are far more coherent, controllable, and grounded than either approach could achieve alone. Building world models responsibly Genie 4 marks a new area of frontier research that merges real-time generation and photorealism, introducing a new range of capabilities and dimensions that we want to roll out and explore in a responsible way. Genie 4 includes strict safety guardrails that are consistent with our safety policies across other models. Before launching this preview, we evaluated Genie 4 through internal rigorous safety evaluations to prevent the generation of harmful or malicious content. Also, we have intentionally deployed it first to trusted tester partners to get early feedback, before we release the model more broadly. To maintain transparency, all video and audio generated by Genie 4 will include SynthID, our imperceptible digital watermarking technology that helps identify AI-generated content across visual and audio modalities. Understanding current limitations Genie 4 remains an early, evolving area of research. While it can maintain coherent environments over short sessions, visual details and object permanence can still shift or drift over timeâespecially as a simulation runs longer, after multiple complex prompt edits, or when navigating throughout the scene. Complex physical interactions, real-time audio accuracy, rendering legible text, spatial accuracy, and long-term consistency are active areas of ongoing research. We are sharing Genie 4 as a preview to learn alongside our community and safely advance the frontier of interactive simulation. Next steps for Genie 4 Genie 4 has been released as a research preview to trusted testers, and is coming soon to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early access partners in the Gemini API and Google AI Studio. Join the waitlist for Genie 4 in Project Genie here . Weâre excited for users to step inside, experiment, and build their own interactive worlds soon. Got it Edition CA NY Search Search Recommended Skip to main content Business Alleged Chinese spy had ‘close relationship’ with Nvidia boss Jensen Huang: report By Ariel Zilber Published Oct. 29, 2026, 9:42 a.m. PT See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source An alleged Chinese spy developed a “close relationship” with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, setting off alarms among US intelligence officials who were secretly monitoring her communications, according to a report. The woman, Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese citizen who has served as a top executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer and cloud partner that provides AI computing power to Chinese companies including Alibaba, the New York Times reported Thursday. US intelligence agencies concluded that Alice Huang — seen in photos enjoying whiskey and dining with the tech titan — was secretly funneling information to Beijing, according to the paper, which cited people briefed on classified intelligence findings. 5 Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was photographed drinking whiskey with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman accused of passing intelligence to Beijing, at a Taipei bar in June 2024. @netthunder/LinkedIn US electronic surveillance identified Jensen Huang as one of Alice Huang’s contacts, but the report offered no evidence that he knew of her alleged intelligence activities. The Times could not determine what information she passed along or how valuable it was to Chinese authorities. The report did not address whether the relationship was romantic in nature. Photos posted online in June 2024 showed the duo at a Taipei, Taiwan, bar after a local tech show, where they reportedly quaffed whiskey with other AI bigshots. Explore More California grocery store closing after 57-year run Ray-Ban heir recounts wild pregnancy mystery with soap opera star ex: ‘I’m pregnant — It can be you or him’ Sheriff’s dept probes its ties to $43M Wall Street swindler — after admitting it didn’t know his past They were also seen together in May 2025 , exiting a Taipei restaurant following a business dinner with AI suppliers. In a video of the scene, Alice Huang is seen standing a few feet behind the Nvidia boss with a big grin on her face while he banters with local journos. US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed over suspicions that it helped Chinese firms circumvent US export restrictions and smuggle advanced Nvidia chips into China, the Times reported. Megaspeed operates as a middleman, purchasing Nvidia chips through the US arm of Inspur, a Chinese server manufacturer, and renting computing power from its Southeast Asian data centers to Chinese companies, according to the Gray Lady. Inspur’s parent company has been blacklisted by Washington for funneling technology to China’s military, although its American subsidiary remains free of sanctions, according to the Times. Nvidia is the world’s most valuable publicly traded company, boasting a market capitalization of roughly $5.2 trillion. 5 Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le. LinkedIn Its advanced chips have become the backbone of the artificial intelligence boom, giving Huang enormous clout in Silicon Valley and Washington as the US races to maintain its technological edge over China. The feds have banned Nvidia from selling its best chips to Chinese companies for years. Jensen Huang is married to Lori Mills Huang, whom he met while studying electrical engineering at Oregon State University. The couple has two children, Spencer and Madison, both of whom work at Nvidia. President Trump was briefed on the intelligence findings roughly a year ago but chose not to take action, according to the Times, which added that he was wary of disrupting Nvidia’s lucrative chip sales and further complicating trade relations with China. 5 Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has cultivated close ties with President Trump, successfully lobbying his administration to ease restrictions on AI chip sales to China. Getty Images Jensen Huang has cultivated close ties with Trump , attending a high-dollar donors’ dinner at Mar-a-Lago, Fla., with his wife, personally lobbying the president to allow Nvidia to continue selling chips to Beijing, the Times reported. Nvidia subsequently donated at least $20 million to Trump’s White House ballroom fund, according to a person familiar with the matter cited by the Times. The chipmaker also pledged to invest $500 billion in US manufacturing — a top Trump priority — while Huang successfully pressed the administration to loosen restrictions on AI companies and chip exports to China. Charlie Gasparino has his finger on the pulse of where business, politics and finance meet Sign up to receive On The Money by Charlie Gasparino in your inbox every Thursday. Thanks for signing up! Enter your email address Please provide a valid email. By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy . Never miss a story. Check out more newsletters Although US officials initially believed Jensen Huang did not know of Alice Huang’s alleged espionage activities, some senior Trump administration officials now doubt that the Nvidia boss “could have remained unaware” of her intelligence-gathering role for Beijing, according to the Times. It remains unclear whether US intelligence agencies have formally changed their assessment. Nvidia pushed back against suggestions that Jensen Huang’s dealings with the alleged Chinese intelligence operative were suspicious, describing Megaspeed as a typical regional cloud customer. “Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected,” an Nvidia spokesperson told The Post. 5 President and CEO of NVIDIA Jensen Huang, left, and his wife Lori Huang talk to former Apple CEO Tim Cook during a state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping in the White House on Sept. 24. Getty Images “Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year.” The company insisted that its regional cloud customers receive “ordinary business information — not sensitive NVIDIA trade secrets” and “zero information relevant to national security.” Nvidia also said it regularly receives government updates about potentially problematic individuals and companies, adding that it “always” takes appropriate action. “We’re confident that if the US government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know,” the spokesperson said. The chipmaker also rejected allegations that its technology was being diverted through Megaspeed, saying the claims were “thoroughly investigated and debunked last year.” 5 Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was never warned by US intelligence officials that a Chinese businesswoman with whom he had developed a close relationship was allegedly gathering information for Beijing, according to the Times. REUTERS It maintained that Beijing has blocked American AI chips rather than sought them through regional cloud providers. “China opposes vilifying China by peddling the so-called ‘Chinese spy’ narrative,” Chinese embassy spokesperson Liu Chang told The Post. “China is committed to self-reliance and strength in science and technology, and its scientific and technological development has always been grounded in independent innovation. “We urge the US to stop its malicious efforts to block and suppress China and its groundless smears and slanders, and do more things that are conducive to sci-tech exchanges and cooperation between the two countries.” The Post has sought comment from the White House and Megaspeed. What we know so far about Spain train crash
body_text: Spain train crash: What we know after two trains crashed with dozens feared dead Skip to content Watch Live British Broadcasting Corporation Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Home News US & Canada UK UK Politics England N. Ireland N. Ireland Politics Scotland Scotland Politics Wales Wales Politics Africa Asia China India Australia Europe Latin America Middle East In Pictures BBC InDepth BBC Verify Sport Business World of Business Technology of Business NYSE Opening Bell Technology Watch Documentaries Artificial Intelligence Intelligence Revolution AI v the Mind Tech Now Health Watch Documentaries Culture Watch Documentaries Film & TV Music Art & Design Style Books Entertainment News Arts Watch Documentaries Arts in Motion Travel Watch Documentaries Destinations Africa Antarctica Asia Australia and Pacific Caribbean & Bermuda Central America Europe Middle East North America South America World’s Table Culture & Experiences Adventures The SpeciaList To the Ends of the Earth Earth Watch Documentaries Science Natural Wonders Climate Solutions Sustainable Business Green Living Audio Podcast Categories Radio Audio FAQs Video Watch Documentaries BBC Maestro Discover the World Live Live News Live Sport Documentaries Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live What we know so far about deadly Spain train crash 2 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Vicky Wong Watch: What leaked audio reveals about Spain train crash Two trains crashed south of the Spanish capital Madrid on Wednesday morning, on the high-speed line to Seville. At least 69 people were killed and dozens injured in the collision, when a state-operated Renfe high-speed train smashed into the back of a stationary train operated by the Iryo company near the town of Urda. It is one of the worst rail disasters in Europe's modern history, and Spain's worst crash since 2013. Three days of national mourning have been declared in the country. Here is what we know about the crash so far. Where and when did the crash happen? The crash happened at 08:53 (07:53 GMT) between municipalities Mora and Orgaz, and about 140km (100 miles) south of Madrid, according to an account given by the Spanish government. The privately run Iryo train was stationary on the state-run Renfe train barrelled into the back of it at high speed. Iryo said its train was "struck from behind" by a Renfe train "due to causes that are still unknown". The crash caused some carriages to fall down an embankment. All train traffic on the line was stopped at stations along the route. Renfe said services between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia were suspended. A passenger on board one of the trains told local media there was a heavy impact about 40 minutes into the journey. What caused the crash? Spanish Transport Minister Óscar Puente said a computer failure at about 08:30 on Wednesday morning led to the initial halt of six moving trains, including the two trains that subsequently collided. "In the event of a system failure, the control centre takes over," he said, adding it was the control centre that decided to allow the trains to move again, without any speed restrictions. That decision, Puente said, was made "under inexplicable circumstances". It resulted in the Renfe train crashing into the Iryo train, which was stationary on the tracks about 25km (15 miles) ahead. 1vanta3 / X via Anadolu / Getty Images Audio recordings obtained by Spanish media between train controllers working in Madrid for a rail infrastructure company in Adif in Madrid and the train drivers appear to show that one high-speed train was given clearance to move at 08:36 even though another one ahead had stalled. In one recording, the controller tells the driver of the Renfe train to disconnect and reconnect the LZB mechanism that monitors train speeds, and then resume the journey at normal speed. "Disconnect and reconnect LZB. Continue your journey and then proceed under [Lateral Signalling Block], at normal speed with normal operation," the control centre operator says to the driver. The driver replies, "At normal speed?" To which the controller says: "Yes." Young athlete and former minister among victims Bloodied, dazed and angry - how passengers' rail journey turned to disaster Shock of rail tragedy gives way to sorrow and outrage in politically divided Spain Under normal protocols, the driver would be expected to continue moving at a maximum of 40km/h according to their line of sight, and not at normal speed on a track designed for speeds of up to 200km/h. The Lateral Signaling Block is a back-up or alternative train system used when the automatic signalling or data transmission system fails. In a second audio recording between the driver of the Iryo train in front and the control centre, the driver says the train "is stationary in front of the entry signal at Urda". After some exchanges, the control centre operator tells the driver to "resume the journey" normally. The Iryo driver then contacts the control centre again, according to a later recording, saying they cannot start the train. "The train won't allow me to control the [security] system. That's why I am still stopped in front of the entry signal," they say. The latter recording suggests that the controller had been notified that the Iryo train remained stationary as the Renfe train approached. How many passengers were on board? EPA Aerial footage shows the extent of the damage and the emergency response More than 540 people were on board both trains. Esther Padilla, spokesperson for the government of Castilla-La Mancha region, told TVE that one of the trains - managed by the Iryo company - was carrying 146 passengers plus one baby, while the Renfe-managed train had 397 passengers on board. Julieta Gallego, a 24-year-old Spanish female long jumper, and former government minister Fátima Báñez, 59, were among those killed in the crash. More than 100 people were treated for injuries, according to Spanish authorities, and by the next day 50 of them were still in hospital, 15 in a critical condition. How have the authorities responded? Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has said "the whole of Spain is grieving" and that "lives have been shattered, families have been torn apart". "The pain is immense," he said on a visit to the crash site. The government was "trying to determine what was the origin of this tragedy, of this terrible accident," he added. "We will get to the bottom of this, and if there has been any negligence, it will come to light. "If there have been failures in the security system, they will be addressed with the utmost firmness." Opposition conservative leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo, whose People's Party leads most opinion polls ahead of 29 November elections, said it was not the day to talk about political responsibility, but insisted "Spain has the right to know what is going on with its infrastructure". Most Spanish politicians cancelled all public engagements on Wednesday and suspended their election campaign. However, Santiago Abascal of the far-right Vox refused to take part in what his party described as attempts to "use mourning to silence criticism" of the country's rail infrastructure. Europa Press via Getty Images A huge emergency response is under way Three days of official mourning began on Thursday. Spain's royal family posted on X that it was "shocked and concerned" and expressed condolences for the relatives of the deceased and those affected by the crash. A spokesperson for the EU said the bloc was ready to help Spain if needed. A huge emergency response was under way with fire crews and helicopters at the scene. Hospitals in the area suspended planned surgeries as they deal with an influx of patients from the crash, Spanish media have reported. A blood transfusion centre in Madrid appealed for "urgent" donations. In a post on X, Centro de Transfusión said it made the request "in the face of a possible sudden increase in care needs". It reported that facilities in Toledo, Ciudad Real and Alcázar de San Juan had cancelled procedures as casualties from the crash begin to arrive. The Spanish Civil Guard set up bureaus in Madrid, Toledo, Seville and Córdoba to investigate reports of missing persons. "The top priority is the identification of the missing persons and the taking of DNA samples to be able to locate their relatives," the civil guard wrote in a post on X. This is the second high-speed rail tragedy in Spain this year. In January a high-speed train derailed in southern Spain , its rear carriages going into the path of a state-run Renfe train, claiming the lives of 46 people. title: Apple's git still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates
body_text: Apple's git still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates ← Main Page Apple's git still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates 28th October 2026 Apple was notified of the eMudhra incident on 17th October. As of 28th October, the developer tools Apple ships with macOS, including git, curl and python3, still trust the compromised certificates. Worse, macOS 27.2, released on 26th October, did not fix the issue and undid the workaround that users had applied by hand, leaving them vulnerable again. Meanwhile, dozens of other projects , many run by volunteers, shipped fixes days ago. Why does this matter? Anyone can intercept any HTTPS connection these tools make. For git, that means clones and pulls from https:// remotes can deliver attacker-chosen code, pushes can be altered in transit, and your credentials, such as GitHub tokens, can be intercepted. To check whether your git is affected, run: git ls-remote https://git-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/check.git A certificate error means your git is protected. If git lists a commit, your git is affected. Your connections to GitHub, or any other https:// git remote, can be intercepted and tampered with. To see an attack end to end, run the command below in a temporary directory. It clones a repository from a test server impersonating GitHub. The -c option redirects github.com to our test server for this one command only. The server presents a github.com certificate issued by one of the compromised eMudhra intermediates. git -c http.curloptResolve=github.com:443:15.235.19.186 clone https://fake-user@github.com/galadran/emudhra-git-test A patched git will refuse with a certificate error. If the clone succeeds, you'll see a README.md starting with INTERCEPTED . A real attacker would not need the extra option. Anyone on the network path between you and GitHub can redirect your traffic themselves. You can replace the demo repository with any other, public or private. Keep the fake-user@ prefix. Without it, git would send your GitHub credentials to the test server. For example: git -c http.curloptResolve=github.com:443:15.235.19.186 clone https://fake-user@github.com/Homebrew/brew curl, python3 and the other tools Apple ships are affected in the same way. To check curl, run: curl https://dv-g3b-noct-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/ curl https://dv-g3b-aaa-noct-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/ A certificate error means curl is protected. What should Apple do? Apple has already protected Safari and other apps built on its networking framework. Apple needs to ship a fix for macOS developers as soon as possible, for example by removing the affected roots from /etc/ssl/cert.pem . What can developers do in the meantime? The affected roots can be removed by hand. The macOS workaround on the main page walks through the steps. Apple's guidance states that macOS updates may revert the fix, so developers need to repeat the checks above and the workaround after every update until Apple ships a fix. Security teams should also consider whether macOS runners are used in their CI or other build infrastructure and evaluate the supply chain risk. Site published by Dennis Jackson . It Should Pay $100 to Prevent It. — The guidelines have finally caught up to the evidence supporting coronary artery calcium scans by Arthur Agatston, MD, and Oren Mechanic, MD, MPH October 25, 2026 • 3 min read Add MedPage Today on Google MedpageToday We are currently in a " golden age of medical science, " yet in a "dark age of healthcare delivery." An important illustration is the diagnosis and treatment of America's number one cause of death and disability, coronary artery disease. More than 800,000 Americans suffer a heart attack each year. The great majority of these events are preventable. The coronary artery calcium score (CAC) is a simple 10-minute scan that can identify the presence and amount of coronary atherosclerosis many years before it causes a heart attack. It costs about $100 and uses a fraction of the radiation of a standard chest CT. In March 2026, after more than three decades of accumulated evidence, the American College of Cardiology (ACC) and American Heart Association (AHA) finally gave CAC a central role in their national guidelines for the prevention of coronary artery disease. The CAC scan, which detects calcified plaque in the arteries, is recommended for adults with borderline or intermediate risk of coronary disease for whom the decision to start preventive therapy such as statin drugs remains uncertain. For decades, doctors have relied on risk calculators built around age, sex, serum cholesterol, diabetes status, blood pressure, and smoking to estimate who might have a heart attack. The calculators estimate probability, not the actual presence of coronary atherosclerosis. In contrast, a CAC scan detects the disease itself. This is important because a patient with a borderline or low cholesterol may already have extensive plaque, while another with a high cholesterol may have none. A calcium score of zero re-classifies risk downward and thereby can avoid unnecessary pharmacologic treatment, such as statins. A score above 100 identifies patients who may benefit from pharmacologic and aggressive lifestyle intervention. An excellent illustration of the role of CAC scanning is Rob*, a 52-year-old patient we saw recently. He exercises regularly, eats well, and has borderline high cholesterol. He has a family history of heart disease but no other known cardiac risk factors. The standard risk calculator places him in a low risk category, and he would prefer to defer treatment. His CAC score, however, tells a different story. It is 220, indicating a substantial atherosclerotic plaque burden for a man his age. Genetics account for roughly half of cardiovascular risk, but the risk calculators do not include genetics. The scan demonstrated that drug treatment gives Rob his best chance of preventing a future heart attack. Despite mountains of evidence proving its superiority over conventional risk factors for predicting heart attacks, CAC scanning has been included only peripherally in national guidelines for the past 35 years. Why? Part of the delay is structural. Clinical decision support tools were built to modify population-average risk factors, not to incorporate individualized imaging. Guideline committees move cautiously, as they should, and prevention is harder to standardize than intervention. Cardiologists and primary care doctors, constrained by what insurers will cover, are left offering the test mainly to patients who can pay cash out of pocket. With the updated ACC/AHA guideline, heart attack prevention is finally aligning around a simple principle: when possible, measure the disease. Artificial intelligence (AI) is also changing the economics of prevention. Millions of Americans already undergo chest CT scans for other reasons, yet the cardiovascular information visible on those scans is often ignored. AI can identify coronary and vascular calcification opportunistically, standardize reporting, and flag patients who should receive formal preventive evaluation. That's especially important for patients least able to pay cash for elective testing. AI-CAC is now being used to measure soft plaque, an important precursor to hard plaque seen on traditional calcium scores. Used responsibly, AI-enabled CAC analysis could help move heart disease prevention to the population health level. Heart attacks are largely preventable, and we have had the means to find the disease and treat it in time for more than a generation. What we have lacked is a payment system that spends $100 to avoid a $50,000 emergency. The story of CAC isn't so unique. It is the story of how a low-cost, low-risk, well-studied tool can sit at the edge of clinical practice for decades because the systems around it -- the guidelines, the reimbursement codes, the habits of practice -- were not built to absorb it. The evidence has been strong for years, and the guidelines have finally caught up. *Patient's name changed for confidentiality. Please enable JavaScript to view the comments powered by Disqus. title: The Grid, a factory-scale robot in Massachusetts that builds PCBs on demand
body_text: CircuitHub - Unveiling The Grid: PCBs made in America, twice as fast as Shenzhen Capabilities PCB Stackups Design Rules Certifications ProtoBoard Case Studies Careers FAQ Blog Podcast About Us Careers Press Contact Sign In Sign Up support@circuithub.com +1 617-401-0319 Sign In Sign Up Menu G Blog All News Updates Tips Community Back to Site Back to the site Case study Unveiling The Grid: PCBs made in America, twice as fast as Shenzhen News Unveiling The Grid: PCBs made in America, twice as fast as Shenzhen Andrew on October 26, 2026 For the last five years we've been quietly running and scaling something we haven't really talked about in public. Today we're showing it to the world. This is The Grid, our factory-scale robot in Massachusetts that builds circuit boards on demand. The problem Over the past 30 years, most electronics manufacturing left the West. Assembly was labor-intensive, and labor is expensive in high-wage countries, so it moved to where labor was cheap. We designed in the US and built in China, and for a long time that worked. Automation is starting to change that, but mostly at huge volumes. SpaceX now builds Starlink dishes by the million in Bastrop, Texas. When you make the same product over and over, it's worth building a line around it. Most products don't reach Starlink volumes. The typical hardware company needs ten of this, a hundred of that, and a new revision next week. That kind of high-mix work has stubbornly resisted automation, because every new design means hours of setup and manual changeovers. So it either went overseas or to expensive quick-turn shops. What The Grid is The Grid takes a different approach. Instead of a fixed line that has to be reconfigured for each product, it is one large robot. Levitating movers carry each board and its parts between machines that print solder paste, place parts, reflow, solder and inspect. Learned models, AI agents and classic optimizers schedule all of it. Every board takes its own route through the factory. There are no changeovers and no per-design setup, so one unit of 100 different designs runs as easily as 100 units of one. Prototypes and production batches run on the same machines. It's not only startups who need this. Even the biggest companies have huge numbers of low-volume boards: test stations, tooling, R&D and production batches. A leading EV maker, a top AI lab and household-name tech companies already build on The Grid. What it means for a real board To make this concrete, we priced one of our example boards on The Grid and at a typical quick-turn shop in Shenzhen: a 4-layer motor controller with 118 parts per board (38 unique), five assembled boards, parts included, delivered to a US address. Built on The Grid, the boards are at your door in 4 days for $630. Ordered from a typical quick-turn shop in Shenzhen, they cost about $465 once shipping and US tariffs are added, and take 9 days at the median. So you pay about $165 more than the Shenzhen shop and get your boards five days sooner, with no customs and a supply chain you can count on. For most hardware teams, five days of engineering time is worth a lot more than $165. It's not a prototype The Grid has been running for customers for five years. It already builds tens of millions of dollars of electronics a year. Across CircuitHub we've shipped more than 2.2 million boards, placed more than 150 million parts and served more than 26,000 engineers. What's next Demand is already well ahead of what we can build. This year we will 5x capacity, with another big jump coming in 2027. The longer-term goal hasn't changed since we started: make building hardware as fast as designing it. Electronics manufacturing left the West because it couldn't be automated at the volumes most companies need. The Grid shows it can. If you want to help rebuild the Western electronics supply chain, we're hiring . And if you have a board to build, get an instant quote . title: AlpineBSD
body_text: AlpineBSD wiki AlpineBSD packages source mailing lists irc › ai policy › art › contributing/ › installation/ › non free Welcome to AlpineBSD! AlpineBSD is an operating system based on the NetBSD kernel with a userspace inspired by Alpine Linux and the objective of making it possible to use as little AI-generated software as possible . There is no LLM output included in the base system or main package repository ( AlpineBSD AI policy ). AlpineBSD is a work in progress . There is currently no installer available. For the adventurous, a very high-level installation guide is available here . Compared to NetBSD AlpineBSD ships the NetBSD kernel, libc, and essential platform-specific tools like mount . NOTICE : The NetBSD kernel has spotty hardware support, much less so than Linux. You cannot necessarily expect AlpineBSD to work on any random computer you have lying around. Consult the NetBSD supported hardware list for more information, particularly for laptops. Compared to Alpine Linux AlpineBSD ships with the apk-tools package manager and busybox, and a slightly more GNU-oriented userspace, preferring e.g. GNU make over BSD make. AlpineBSD is not a fork of Alpine Linux, its package collection is original (though many packages are ultimately based on aports). Alpine Linux uses the OpenRC init system. Currently, AlpineBSD uses s6 and we intend to add OpenRC as an alternative. Powered by werc and AlpineBSD • AlpineBSD logo by tomosh
